a.xlink:title: Base class for all Ecstasy statements.
An assert statement.
An assignment statement specifies an l-value, an assignment operator, and an r-value.
A case statement.
A "catch" statement.
Represents a statement that corresponds to a Component in an Ecstasy FileStructure.
A conditional statement, including "if", "while", etc.
An expression statement is just an expression that someone stuck a semicolon on the end of.
A "goto" statement is any statement that impacts the control flow of the program by jumping from the ...
An import statement specifies a qualified name to alias as a simple name.
A labeled statement represents a statement that has a label.
This represents multiple variable declarations in a list.
A return statement specifies a return with optional values.
A block statement specifies a series of statements.
A "try" or "using" statement.
A variable declaration statement specifies a type and a simple name for a variable.
Common base class for all statements and expressions.
A method declaration.
A property declaration.
A type declaration.
A typedef statement specifies a type to alias as a simple name.
A synthetic MethodDeclarationStatement that contains the eval body.
An "Iterable"-based "for" statement.
The traditional "for" statement.
An "if" statement.
A "switch" statement.
A "while" or "do while" statement.
A break statement represents the "break" keyword.
A continue statement represents the "continue" keyword.
